title: Questions written for their own text
statement: Write each question for its own text and teach no rule of thumb many texts break, such as checking the title or expecting the meaning or evidence in one sentence.
detail: In the reading course's third review round, a generic routine, find the one sentence the story is about and check it against the title, was judged bad advice: a fable's meaning is a synthesis, and titles often don't tell the main idea. The course's response made questions bespoke to the text a rule, and its red-team taxonomy now checks both for generic questions and for the misconception they taught, that text evidence is a single sentence when it is often two ideas from different places (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`, lines 79-80).
